name: Potential Reverse Shell
description: This rule detects the creation of a reverse shell by analyzing a sequence of auditd events, including the execution of suspicious commands followed by network activity and shell creation. Reverse shells are often used by attackers to gain persistent remote access to a compromised system.
note:
Investigation Steps

- Review the process execution details to identify the path and name of the suspicious executable.
- Investigate the parent process to determine if it was launched by a legitimate shell.
- Analyze the network activity, focusing on the destination IP address.
- Check the process tree for a new shell spawned after the network connection.
- Investigate the user account under which the suspicious process was executed.
- Correlate timestamps of events to understand the sequence of actions.
false_positives: Legitimate administrative scripts may initiate network connections.
Automated deployment tools might use networking calls.
Create exceptions for known safe processes.
query:
sequence with maxspan=300s
[process where event.module == "auditd" and 
  auditd.log.SYSCALL == "execve" and 
  (
    process.executable in ("/usr/bin/wget") or
    process.args : ("*-O- *", "*|bash*", "*|sh*")
  )
]
[process where event.module == "auditd" and 
  auditd.log.SYSCALL == "execve" and 
  process.executable in ("/usr/bin/bash", "/usr/bin/sh")
]
[process where event.module == "auditd" and 
  auditd.log.SYSCALL in ("socket", "connect")
]
